Weighted sampling with removal, restore, and AVX512 fast paths using a radix-9 tree.

# Purpose
`fd_wsample.c` implements a weighted sampling data structure that supports random selection by weight, with and without removal. It uses a flat radix-`9` tree stored in shared memory, with cumulative subtree sums in each internal node. The file defines the private sampler state, memory layout rules, alignment and footprint helpers, construction and teardown functions, and the core sampling logic. It also supports restoring the full tree state after deletions when `restore_enabled` is set.

The main operations are [`fd_wsample_sample`](<#fd_wsample_sample>), [`fd_wsample_sample_and_remove`](<#fd_wsample_sample_and_remove>), [`fd_wsample_remove_idx`](<#fd_wsample_remove_idx>), and the `_many` variants. Sampling uses a `fd_chacha_rng_t` random generator and maps a uniform query into a tree path by comparing against stored left sums. Removal updates the cumulative sums along the path to the removed leaf. The file also contains AVX-512 code paths for the `R==9` case, plus fallback scalar code, and it handles poisoned sampling state through `poisoned_weight` and `poisoned_mode`.
